metadata.title: COVID-19 RESEARCH RESOURCES IN PIRLS 2021
metadata.venue: Boston College, TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This report is a PIRLS 2021 COVID-19 contextual resources guide rather than an empirical model-estimation study. It describes which PIRLS 2021 instruments contain COVID-19-related items (Home, School, and Curriculum/Encyclopedia contributions) and how some items were adapted for countries with delayed assessment schedules. Because the report does not present an analytic model with an estimation target, it does not specify whether complex survey weights (e.g., student sampling weights and replicate weights) were applied. For users conducting secondary analyses with PIRLS 2021 microdata, the appropriate approach is to apply the PIRLS 2021 complex survey design weights and replicate weights provided in the International Database when estimating population-representative statistics and standard errors.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because this document does not estimate or model PIRLS reading achievement PVs; it documents and summarizes COVID-19 contextual questionnaire items and reporting considerations. Missing-data handling is not reported because the report does not run an analysis pipeline that would require an explicit missing-data strategy (e.g., imputation or deletion) for model estimation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report does not define an analytic subsample for model estimation. Instead, it documents PIRLS 2021 COVID-19 contextual items and presents international-average percentages and country-level reporting for those items. For some Home and School questionnaire items, the report explains that responses are treated as 'Not Applicable' when a filter condition is not met (e.g., if the parent reported the child did not stay home due to COVID-19, subsequent COVID-19 home items are not answered). For cross-country comparability, it also notes that some countries delayed data collection and administered PIRLS to a different cohort timing (full-year delay or about half-year delay), which affects how PIRLS 2021 results should be interpreted for trends.

data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS 2021 Insights report compiles COVID-19-related contextual resources available in the PIRLS 2021 International Database. It explains that PIRLS 2021 reading achievement results cannot be used for causal inference about COVID-19 learning loss, but the contextual questionnaires support descriptive and within-country analyses of pandemic-related schooling conditions. The report details three instrument sources: the Home Questionnaire (parent/guardian reports on staying home, home-based learning resources, and perceived learning progress), the School Questionnaire (principal reports on disruption duration and remote-learning resources/supports), and the Curriculum/Encyclopedia contributions (country-level policy and practice descriptions of closures, decision-making, distance learning modalities, and supports). It also highlights comparability issues due to COVID-19-driven modifications to the PIRLS 2021 data collection timeline, including full-year and half-year delays for some countries. Finally, it provides item-level caveats such as filter logic and response-option limitations (e.g., ceiling effects for disruption duration).
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a contextual resources and reporting guide rather than an empirical ML study. It does not estimate predictive models, does not report PV-based achievement modeling, and does not provide an analytic sample definition for statistical inference. As a result, fields related to ML techniques, model performance, and conceptual predictors are intentionally empty, while the report focuses on instrument content, item logic, and interpretation guidance for secondary analyses.
